name: Electrochemical Vapor Seeding Drone EVSD-4 'Rainmaker'
description:
The EVSD-4 is a medium-frame area-preparation drone that disperses a proprietary electrochemical vapor compound across a target zone, seeding the atmosphere with ionized particulate that dramatically enhances the conductivity and lethality of subsequent electrical or galvanic weapon discharges. The vapor—a suspension of hygroscopic metallic salt particles developed by OUROBOROS ENERGY for industrial capacitor humidification—bonds to airborne moisture and settles on surfaces, clothing, and exposed skin, creating an invisible conductive network that bridges gaps between targets and dramatically lowers the energy threshold required for electrical disruption.

The Rainmaker operates at low altitude (3–15 meters) to ensure dense, even vapor distribution before ascending to observation altitude. Once a zone has been seeded, galvanic or electrical weapons discharged into it experience dramatically amplified arc propagation—discharges that would normally affect a single target can chain to adjacent persons, and energy weapons operating at sub-lethal settings become lethal within the seeded zone. The vapor disperses naturally within 4–8 minutes in open air or up to 20 minutes in enclosed spaces, giving operators a defined engagement window.

OUROBOROS ENERGY developed the vapor compound for entirely non-military purposes, but RINGO CORPONATION's defense subsidiary recognized its weaponization potential and quietly funded EVSD-4 platform development through a series of subsidiary arrangements. The resulting weapon exists in a legal gray zone: the drone itself is classified as an 'atmospheric preparation system' with no offensive designation, while the vapor compound retains its industrial certification. This regulatory gap has made the EVSD-4 surprisingly accessible through legitimate industrial supply channels.
legality: Restricted (regulatory gray zone — platform licensed as industrial equipment)
specifications:
frame dimensions: 620mm x 580mm x 200mm
weight: 4.1 kg (full vapor reservoir)
vapor reservoir capacity: 1.8 liters suspension
effective seeding area: ~200 square meters per full reservoir
seeding altitude: 3–15 meters operational
vapor persistence: 4–8 minutes open air, up to 20 minutes enclosed
arc propagation enhancement: Estimated 3–5x standard electrical discharge range within seeded zone
operational endurance: 35 minutes on internal cell
vapor compound designation: OUROBOROS Type-7 Hygroscopic Metallic Suspension
tactical_use: Operators deploy the EVSD-4 30–60 seconds before committing to an engagement, seeding the target zone while maintaining cover. Once the vapor has distributed, any electrical or galvanic weapon becomes dramatically more effective—standard-issue galvanic sidearms can chain across groups, and area-denial emitters achieve full coverage at reduced power settings. Teams operating with hardened, insulated equipment gain a significant asymmetric advantage in seeded environments. Counter-tactics focus on either dispersing the vapor (high-velocity fans, rapid ventilation) or detecting the drone before seeding completes. The vapor is colorless but has a faint metallic smell that experienced operators recognize.
cultural_context: The EVSD-4's industrial legal classification has made it a favorite of operators who want military-grade area preparation without the legal exposure of prohibited hardware. Corporate security consultants treat it as a 'force multiplier' in the euphemistic language of their industry briefings. In Meridian 88's street-level conflict culture, 'calling rain' before a hit has become slang for thorough, professional preparation—implying the operator has resources, planning capability, and access to specialized equipment. Electrical weapon specialists—colloquially known as 'stormcallers'—prize the EVSD-4 as the cornerstone of their operational doctrine.
known_users: Corporate security consultants operating in gray-legal space
Industrial sabotage operatives using legitimate procurement channels
story_hooks: A warehouse fire investigation reveals traces of OUROBOROS Type-7 suspension in the debris—the fire was electrical in origin and someone used a Rainmaker to turn a standard arc discharge into a mass casualty event.

A player character notices a faint metallic smell in the corridor ahead—someone has pre-seeded the zone and is waiting with electrical weapons. The drone is still overhead, and disabling it before it completes a second seeding pass becomes an urgent priority.

OUROBOROS ENERGY's legal team has finally noticed the weaponized use of their industrial compound and is preparing to file a regulatory complaint that would close the gray market—RINGO CORPONATION wants the filing delayed or buried, and is looking for leverage against the OUROBOROS executive leading the effort.
